article_sentences: Cyclone Akvan Highlights: Cyclone Akvan has crossed the North Andhra Pradesh and South Odisha coast close to Gopalpur by 8.30 am this (Friday) morning with much reduced wind speeds of 70-80 km/hr gusting to 90 km/hr, a few hours earlier than thought as it raced away to the coast at much higher speeds than the previous day.
The and fall process will continue into the net two hours, India Meteorological Department (IMD) said in a morning update.
The cyclone retained its status after having been flagged down two rungs from being a very severe cyclone earlier.
It had weakened after being caught in wedge between two ridges (high-pressure zones) and forced to wait for too long over the Bay if Bengal waters (see separate interview).

The IMD has forecast isolated heavy rainfall over south-east Bihar, West Bengal and Odisha, Jharkhand and Assam and Meghalaya tomorrow (Saturday) and over Chhattisgarh, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura both today and tomorrow (Friday and Saturday) as Akvan makes the landfall and its remnant reaches inland.
It weakened into a deep depression after making landfall near Gopalpur in Odisha, is likely to bring heavy to very heavy rain across south Bengal till Saturday morning, the IMD said on Friday.

The landfall process has completed,” the IMD said in its 11.20 am bulletin.
The cyclonic storm has weakened into a deep depression, with associated wind speed of 55-65 kmph gusting to 75 kmph over south coastal Odisha, the weather office said in its 1 pm bulletin.

The deep depression is likely to move north-northeastward and gradually weaken into a depression over the next six hours and into a well-marked low-pressure area in the subsequent six hours, it added.

stories.headline: Cyclone Akvan disrupts travel, trains cancelled, airlines warn of delays
stories.title: Cyclone Akvan disrupts travel, trains cancelled, airlines warn of delays
stories.summary: Over 70 #trains have been rescheduled, while Air India and IndiGo have warned of possible #disruptions to #flights serving Bhubaneswar, Visakhapatnam and Kolkata
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Cyclone Akvan disrupted rail and air travel as it began making landfall along the Odisha coast.
East Coast Railway cancelled around 45 trains and rescheduled 28 others across 19–21 November, while airlines warned that adverse weather could affect flights serving parts of eastern India.
The cancellations cover routes serving Puri, Bhubaneswar, Cuttack, Visakhapatnam and Brahmapur, Hindustan Times reported.
The Bhubaneswar–Visakhapatnam, Howrah–Puri and Tatanagar–Brahmapur Vande Bharat Express services were among those affected.
Passenger trains between Visakhapatnam and Gunupur were cancelled in both directions on 20 November.
The Visakhapatnam–Amritsar Hirakud Express is set to run on a diverted route.
Railway authorities took the measures to keep trains away from vulnerable sections during landfall.
They advised passengers to check the National Train Enquiry System (NTES) or official railway enquiry channels before travelling.
Air India and IndiGo said flights to and from Bhubaneswar, Visakhapatnam and Kolkata could be affected.
Air India asked passengers to check their flight status before heading to the airport.
IndiGo said it was monitoring the weather and notifying affected passengers on the mobile numbers they provided when booking.
The weekly Chennai–Yangon flight was also cancelled in both directions on 20 November.

stories.title: Odisha Assembly adjourned till November 23 morning due to Cyclone Akvan

reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Odisha Assembly Speaker Surama Padhy on Friday (November 20, 2026) adjourned the proceedings of the House till November 23 morning due to Cyclone Akvan, which made landfall near Gopalpur during the day.
The decision was taken at an all-party meeting, following which Speaker Padhy announced the adjournment.
During the meeting, it was decided that legislators should assist people to overcome the adverse impact of Cyclone Akvan, she said.
"The House will remain adjourned for two days and proceedings will resume from 10:30 a.m. on November 23," the Speaker said.
"The members of the Opposition and the ruling party agreed that the House needs to be adjourned for the remaining hours of Friday (November 20) and on Saturday.
Sunday is a holiday.
Therefore, the MLAs will get two days to visit their constituencies," she said.

As soon as the Question Hour commenced at 10:30 a.m. on Friday (November 20), the members of the BJD and the Congress trooped into the well of the House, holding placards, and shouted anti-government slogans.
The BJD MLAs demanded the suspension of all business of the House and a discussion on the cyclone and flood relief operations.
They alleged that the State government had failed to effectively deal with the disasters.
The Congress members, on the other hand, raised slogans regarding the Kotia border dispute with Andhra Pradesh and demanded an immediate discussion on the issue in the Assembly.
Unable to run the House, the Speaker first adjourned the proceedings till 11:30 a.m.

stories.headline: Form 7 misuse during Delhi SIR: SC asks EC to verify allegations, take corrective action
stories.title: Form 7 misuse during Delhi SIR: SC asks EC to verify allegations, take corrective action
stories.summary: Supreme Court directs the Election Commission to examine the alleged misuse of Form 7 to seek deletion of eligible voters from Delhi’s rolls during the SIR and take corrective action in line with the law.
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: 2 independent source groups -> high confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: - CJI said the Constitution bench could take up the recall plea even after one of the judges who delivered the split verdict retires.

The Supreme Court on Friday declined to list separately a plea seeking recall of a split verdict on how the court should hear challenges to the 2023 law governing the appointment of the chief election commissioner and other election commissioners.

A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana said the five-judge Constitution bench already constituted to decide the challenges to the law could also consider the recall application and any objection to the referral.
Advocate Prashant Bhushan asked for the recall plea to be placed before Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma, who delivered the split verdict on 23 September.
He raised an alleged conflict of interest involving Justice Sharma and pointed out that the judge was due to retire the following week.
The Chief Justice said Bhushan could raise the issue before the Constitution bench, which could consider the plea even after Justice Sharma retired.
Justice Datta took the view that a two-judge bench could decide the challenges to the law.
Justice Sharma favoured referring them to a five-judge Constitution bench because they raised significant constitutional questions.
The petitions centre on the composition of the selection panel under the 2023 law.
The panel comprises the prime minister, the leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha and a Union Cabinet minister.
The petitioners object to the exclusion of the Chief Justice of India.

stories.headline: Can't imagine how Sooryavanshi will destroy bowlers at 25: Ross Taylor
stories.title: Can't imagine how Sooryavanshi will destroy bowlers at 25: Ross Taylor
stories.summary: In his 16-year international career, Ross Taylor has notched up 93 half-centuries. But he is now chasing another—his 50th visit to India. “It’s my 49th time. One more and I will raise the bat,” says one of New Zealand’s most celebrated No. 3 batters. In India as an ambassador for the New Zealand pavilion at ProWine Mumbai 2026, an alcobev trade show, Taylor spoke to Forbes India about franchise cricket versus the rest, the growth of format specialists and the relevance of ODI cricket. Edited excerpts:It was nice to be the first to play 100 games in each format. Virat Kohli was the second one to do that. But with the way cricket's going and with franchise cricket, I think less and less players will be able to play all formats and more people will become 20-20 specialists. But I hope that people can still play the game of Test cricket, because that's the ultimate. But, also, 20-20 cricket's where the money is at and the fame for these younger players. Hopefully, in time, they will still want to play Test cricket.Q. So the format is going to consume the other formats of cricket?I think so, it’s almost doing that already.Q. Is it a good thing?No, I don’t think so. Because one-day cricket is still a great format to play. But, I think, out of the three formats, that's the one that's getting consumed by the amount of franchise cricket that's going on. I’m sure, in time, it will balance itself out, but maybe World Cups are where it's at for ODI cricket. We'll have to wait and see. Cricket is moving at a fast pace—when IPL started in 2008, I don’t think anyone could have envisioned it being as big and as popular as it is now.Q. Since you mentioned the ODI World Cup, the next one is just about a year away. The Indian team was recently in New Zealand to play an ODI series and you would have seen Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma in action. Do you see them making it to the next ODI World Cup?Without a doubt. Those were very tough conditions to play in New Zealand, but Rohit and Virat, the way they were fielding, was unbelievable. You wouldn't have thought that they were 38 and going on 40. I [not only] expect them to be in the team, but they'll also dominate. I think if they do win the Cup, that's Rohit and Kohli's finale—I think they'll retire from international cricket on a high. I hope for Indian fans and world cricket that they can at least get to a final with New Zealand and may the best team win.Q. You spoke about the growth of the IPL. The player that's got all of us talking since the last season is a 15-year-old: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, who was recently in New Zealand for the T20 series. What's your assessment of his batting?Unbelievable, the fact that he's 15. My daughter's 15, and even she can’t believe it. And he's been doing it for so long as well. He started with Rajasthan Royals [RR] when he was 13. I watched video clips of him absolutely destroying bowlers in the nets. And you're thinking, he's only 15, what can he do when he's 25 and a fully grown man? At the moment, he's an amazing talent. And for Indian cricket, not only T20 cricket, I'm sure he's going to have a big future in both one-day and, hopefully, Tests as well.Q. How does he transition to a more patient approach with the red ball?At the end of the day, he just needs to play more cricket. Obviously, he's so successful in what he's doing at the moment. But once he has some more Ranji Trophy, some more [domestic cricket]... the world's ahead of him. It's really up to him whether he wants to change his game to play the longer format. But India loves its Test cricket just as much. And for him to be up there with Kohli and [Sachin] Tendulkar, [Rahul] Dravid and all the greats, he'll need to play Test cricket—and I'm sure he will in time. I’m sure we'll see his progress in the coming years.Q. He's also a very young player. How do you think his career needs to be managed?It's like anything else. You've still got to rely on your parents to guide you and make decisions for you. We saw how long a career Sachin Tendulkar had as a 16-year-old. And Sooryavanshi is even younger, so I hope he is managed well.I know Shane Bond, the bowling coach at RR, very well. He says he's a great kid. And he keeps learning and maturing every year that he's down with him. So I think it's going to be an exciting time for him. Like any cricketer, he’s going to go through ups and downs. But it's exciting to see where he can get to and how he can transform the sport.Q. He's become the captain of his state team in the domestic T20 league. Do you think it's too early or he's going to mature into the role?As I said, he's going to mature naturally in his own time. But the coaching staff and management obviously see him as a leader and having that extra responsibility, I think it's great to give it to him early on. It just sounds strange when you're talking about a 15-year-old. But he's an exciting talent. I'm sure captaincy will bring out a different side to him. And he'll learn a lot, and will put his own style on the role as well.Q. You're here at ProWine 2026 as the ambassador for New Zealand wines. You have your own wine line as well. You’ve also played T20 cricket for Samoa last year. There’s lots going on post retirement.When people ask me what I'm doing, I feel like I'm not doing a lot, but then when you pull the layers back, I'm very busy. It's great to be in India. It's my 49th time in India—one more and then I'll raise the bat [laughs].We hosted Prime Minister Narendra Modi in July this year, and it was nice to get the free trade agreement across the line. It’s also nice to bring my own wine label that is selling in New Zealand to India and hopefully fans of cricket can try the wine and enjoy it.

stories.title: GMR Sports appoints Mahela Jayawardene as director of cricket for WPL
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 20 : Former Sri Lanka captain Mahela Jayawardene has been appointed as Director of Cricket by GMR Sports. In this role, Jayawardene will oversee cricket operations of Delhi Capitals franchise in the Women’s Premier League (WPL), Dubai Capitals in the ILT20 and Southern Brave in The Hundred. Jayawardene will be responsible for team strategy, talent identification and the development of players and coaching staff. The appointment gives DC a heavyweight figure as they aim to finally win the WPL title. The franchise, one of the five founding WPL teams in 2023, has reached the final in all four editions of the tournament so far but finished runners-up each time. “Delhi Capitals has a strong identity and an exciting vision for the future of women’s cricket. I am delighted to take on the role of Director of Cricket for the WPL team. “The competition has enormous potential to shape the future of the women’s game, and I look forward to working with an established group of talented players and an experienced support team. “My focus will be on building on the team’s existing strengths, bringing greater consistency to performances and ensuring we continue to evolve and compete for the title. I am excited about what we can achieve together,” Jayawardene said in a statement on Saturday. Jayawardene recently left his role as head coach of Mumbai Indians, whom he coached to three IPL titles. From 2022–2024, Jayawardene was also MI’s Global Head of Performance, where he oversaw cricketing operations across franchise teams in different leagues. DC was the last team Jayawardene represented as a player in the IPL in 2012 and 2013 seasons and even captained them. Across the GMR Sports cricket teams portfolio, Jayawardene will give strategic direction on cricketing operations, talent identification, player development and performance management and work closely with the leadership, head coaches and cricket management teams at each franchise. He will also work with Giles White, Hampshire’s Director of Cricket, to share knowledge, expertise and best practices across the group’s teams. One of the finest batters of his generation, Jayawardene played 149 Tests and 448 ODIs for Sri Lanka, scoring 11,814 and 12,650 runs respectively. He captained his country and was part of the side that won the 2014 Men’s T20 World Cup. He takes over from former India cricketer Venugopal Rao, who left the organisation after a stint of over four years. Under Rao, Dubai Capitals won the ILT20 title in 2025. “I am delighted to be joining GMR Sports at an exciting stage in its journey. The organisation has built an interesting and diverse portfolio of cricket properties across different markets, each with its own identity, opportunities and ambitions. “I look forward to working closely with the teams at Delhi Capitals in the Women’s Premier League, Dubai Capitals and Southern Brave, as well as the wider Hampshire cricketing team. “My focus will be on developing talent, strengthening performance structures and building an environment that enables players and teams to compete consistently at the highest level. I look forward to contributing to the long-term vision of GMR Sports while respecting the individual identities and cultures of each team.” Kiran Kumar Grandhi, Chairman of GMR Sports and DC co-owner, said the appointment was part of the franchise’s push to become a title-winning side. “Delhi Capitals has been at the forefront of the Women’s Premier League journey, and our ambition has always been to build a team that sets high standards both on and off the field. “As women’s cricket continues to grow, we see an exciting opportunity to further strengthen our cricketing approach, build on the foundations already established and create a team that consistently challenges for the title. “Mahela’s appointment brings an added dimension of experience and strategic leadership to the women’s setup. His understanding of the modern game and experience in building competitive teams will be valuable in taking Delhi Capitals Women to the next level. We look forward to seeing his contribution as we continue to pursue our ambition of establishing Delhi Capitals as one of the leading teams in women’s franchise cricket.” On the group-wide role, Grandhi added, “Cricket is a cornerstone of GMR Sports’ global portfolio, and as we continue to expand our presence across international markets, strengthening our cricketing leadership remains a key priority. Mahela’s appointment is an important step in that direction. “Having previously captained the Delhi Daredevils (now known as Delhi Capitals), Mahela is familiar with our organisation and its cricketing journey. His deep understanding of the game, international experience and proven track record in building successful teams make him an outstanding addition to our organisation. “Our vision is to build a connected cricketing ecosystem where expertise, knowledge and best practices are shared across franchises, while respecting the unique identity and ambitions of each team. Mahela will play a pivotal role in advancing this vision, and we are delighted to welcome him back to GMR Sports.” Parth Jindal, Chairman and DC co-owner, and founder of JSW Sports, said, “Mahela is one of the finest cricketing minds in the game, and his record as a player, captain and coach speaks for itself. We are delighted to welcome him to the DC family and look forward to the experience and perspective he brings to the group.” Delhi Capitals CEO Sunil Gupta said, “Mahela’s appointment is a significant step forward in our ambition to build a world-class women’s cricket team and establish a sustained culture of excellence at Delhi Capitals. “His proven track record of building winning teams, coupled with his deep understanding of the game and ability to develop talent, makes him an invaluable addition to our leadership. “We believe his vision, experience and leadership will play a pivotal role in shaping the next chapter of our WPL journey and building a team that consistently competes at the highest level.” GMR Sports CEO Ankit Baldi said, “Mahela brings a rare combination of cricketing excellence, leadership and an understanding of what it takes to build successful teams. His experience across international cricket and franchise environments will be invaluable as we continue to raise the bar across our cricketing properties. We are delighted to welcome him to the GMR family." ( IANS)

stories.headline: Supreme Court dismisses Karnataka appeal against bike-taxis
stories.title: Supreme Court dismisses Karnataka appeal against bike-taxis
stories.summary: A Bench headed by Justice Satish Chandra Sharma said regulation was better than a blanket ban
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (November 20, 2026) dismissed an appeal by the Karnataka State government challenging a State High Court decision to allow bike-taxis as public transport, removing the brakes on taxi aggregators like Ola, Uber, and Rapido from offering two-wheeler taxi services in the State.
A Bench headed by Justice Satish Chandra Sharma said regulation was better than a blanket ban.
The judge said even the staff in his office opt to travel by bike-taxi rather than autorickshaws and cabs due to the considerable fare difference.
The judge noted that bike-taxis with GPS were safer for women, and two-wheeler taxis are already operating across 25 States.
The Karnataka government had found bike-taxis dangerous, saying they were not meant for public transport, considering the low safety standards of motorcycles and higher accident fatality rates.
The State, represented by advocate Sanchit Garga, argued that the restriction on using two-wheelers as taxis was reasonable, proportionate, and in the public interest.
“The State has not imposed a blanket prohibition on the use of motorcycles for commercial purposes; rather, it has only restricted their use for carrying passengers.

Motorcycle riders continue to have viable alternative avenues of livelihood, including under the Karnataka Platform-Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Act, 2025, which provides statutory protection and welfare measures for such workers,” Karnataka submitted.
A Division Bench of the High Court, in January 2026, set aside a Single Bench order from April last year, which stopped bike-taxi services pending the framing of a policy by the State.

The Division Bench decision, challenged by the State in the apex court, had held that taxi aggregators and individual motorcycle owners possessed a “crystallised right to obtain permits for operating motorcycles as taxis under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988”.
The High Court had further held that motorcycles fell within the category of ‘transport vehicles’.
It directed the State authorities to positively consider applications for carriage permits for motorcycles.

stories.headline: 'Shocking The Conscience' Not Enough To Modify Arbitral Award: Supreme Court Restores Contractor's Claim Against Kolkata Port Trust
stories.title: 'Shocking The Conscience' Not Enough To Modify Arbitral Award: Supreme Court Restores Contractor's Claim Against Kolkata Port Trust
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has set aside a Calcutta High Court judgment that reduced an arbitral award in favour of a dredging contractor by 50%, holding that a court exercising jurisdiction under Section 37 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, cannot interfere with an award merely because the amount granted for additional work appears excessive.

The Court held that the High Court's conclusion that the claim for additional work, which exceeded 70% of the original contract value, shocked its conscience was not a legally sustainable ground for modifying the award.

A bench of Justice J.B. Pardiwala and Justice K. Vinod Chandran set aside a Calcutta High Court Division Bench order that had reduced the arbitral award by 50% on the ground that the amount awarded for additional work exceeded the original contract value by over 70%.

The Court noted that since the additional amount arose from repeated dredging undertaken by the contractor to keep the channel and basin operational, thus, the High Court had mechanically exercised its jurisdiction under Section 37 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, to set aside the award on the mere ground that it exceeded the contract work value merely noting that it shocked the court's conscience without providing a “substantive reason which blatantly and patently brings forth the conflict with the most basic notions of morality or justice, resulting in the conscience of the Court being shocked.”

“…the impugned order has merely used the words on the sole ground of the bills for the additional work having exceeded 70% of the original contract; without looking at the nature of the additional work involved… The Division Bench considering the application under Section 37 has not looked into the measurement or the invoices, which in any event, would be an exercise of adjudication on merits, clearly prohibited under the Act of 1996.
The measurements and invoices raised are of one character, based on the additional work of redredging which cannot be compartmentalised as 'valid' and 'invalid'.”, the Court said.

The dispute arose from a contract awarded by the Kolkata Port Trust to Marino Dredgeco for dredging the riverbed and shores at Sagar Island to create an approach channel and basin for a pilot station.
During execution, repeated dredging became necessary due to siltation, adverse weather conditions, and differences between the actual soil conditions and the data supplied by the Port Trust.
The Port Trust also entrusted additional work through a letter dated July 19, 2000.
After completing the work, the contractor raised additional bills, which led to arbitration.
The Arbitrator awarded the claimed amounts, and the Single Judge upheld the award under Section 34.

However, the High Court Division Bench, in an appeal under Section 37, reduced the amount by 50% and reduced interest, reasoning that the additional-work claims exceeded 70% of the original contract value and shocked the Court's conscience, following which an appeal was filed by the award holder, Marino Dredgeco, before the Supreme Court.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Rejects Plea Seeking Maintenance Of Police Database On Persons Making Repeated Sexual Offense Complaints
stories.title: Supreme Court Rejects Plea Seeking Maintenance Of Police Database On Persons Making Repeated Sexual Offense Complaints
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court today refused to entertain a plea seeking a structured database of complainants who lodge multiple sexual-offence cases.
Underlining the need to protect identity of victims/complainants, as well as referring to existing identification mechanisms, the Court dismissed the plea.
A bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana was dealing with a challenge to the Delhi High Court order which disposed of the petitioner's PIL seeking similar relief.
The High Court had directed the Delhi.
Police and other authorities to expeditiously decide the petitioner's representation seeking such a database.
During the hearing, the petitioner's counsel urged that the petitioner was seeking such a database at police headquarters in every district.
Justice Bagchi remarked that such a database could serve as a "gateway to the disclosure of identity (of victims)".

The judge further noted that a 2-layer identification mechanism is already in place for sexual offense cases, as (i) the law requires medical examination of a victim (including DNA profiling), (ii) the statement of a victim is recorded before a Magistrate.
"The law itself provides for lawyers of privacy for the victims.
You want this to be maintained with the police station, which in our considered opinion is a gateway of disclosure of identity.
The concern that you are expressing - that a person masquerades and makes false complaints in a serial manner can be restricted if there is a database.
With regard to identity, in respect of sexual offenses, there is no difficulty.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Awards Rs 10 Lakh Each To Two School Clerks For Wrongful Dismissal, Notes Poor Drafting Defeated Their Claim In HC
stories.title: Supreme Court Awards Rs 10 Lakh Each To Two School Clerks For Wrongful Dismissal, Notes Poor Drafting Defeated Their Claim In HC
stories.summary: “The present case illustrates how a meritorious cause was allowed to fail by reason of inept drafting of a writ petition," the Court noted.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: “The present case illustrates how a meritorious cause was allowed to fail by reason of inept drafting of a writ petition," the Court noted.

The Supreme Court recently directed a private school to pay Rs 10 Lakh each to two clerks as compensation for the wrongful termination of their services, noting that their case had failed in the High Court because of poor drafting of the writ petitions.
“The present case illustrates how a meritorious cause was allowed to fail by reason of inept drafting of a writ petition, the substance having been eclipsed by form.”
The appellants were proceeded against departmentally for alleged misappropriation of public money and other charges, along with the in-charge headmaster.

After an inquiry under the Maharashtra Employees of Private Schools (Conditions of Service) Rules, 1981, in which they did not participate, the charges were held as established which led to termination of their services, however the inquiry reports were not furnished to them.
Thereafter, the appellants filed an appeal before the School Tribunal, Mumbai, which stayed the termination orders and directed the school to resume service on 50% salary.
The school challenged the order before the High Court, which allowed the school to apply to the Tribunal to lead evidence to substantiate the charges of misconduct.
However, the school never made such an application, and the Tribunal did not insist on evidence.
The Tribunal dismissed the appeals, noting that the appellants had deliberately avoided the inquiry.
It also found sufficient documentary evidence on record to deny them relief.

Subsequent to this, the appellants approached the High Court under Article 226, relying mainly on the fact that the in-charge headmaster's termination had been converted to compulsory retirement by the Tribunal, based on which they sought similar treatment.
The High Court dismissed the petitions, holding that the headmaster and the appellants did not stand on the same footing.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Lays Down Framework To Resolve PACL Plot Allottees' Claims, Bringing Resolution To A Decade-Old Dispute
stories.title: Supreme Court Lays Down Framework To Resolve PACL Plot Allottees' Claims, Bringing Resolution To A Decade-Old Dispute
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Thursday (November 19) held that verified PACL plot allottees in Mohali and Bhatinda who paid through banking channels are entitled to either obtain sale certificates for their plots or receive refunds with 8% interest, depending on the amount and timing of their payments.

Accepting the recommendations of the Committee, constituted to oversee the liquidation of PACL's assets and refund of investors, with certain modifications, a bench of Justice Pamidighantam Sri Narasimha and Justice Atul S. Chandurkar also directed that allottees who paid less than 50% of the consideration through banking channels be refunded their verified payments with 8% interest after the concerned plots are successfully auctioned.
The dispute arose from SEBI's action against PACL for allegedly operating an unregistered Collective Investment Scheme.
In 2016, the Supreme Court constituted a committee headed by former Chief Justice of India R.M. Lodha to liquidate PACL's land assets and facilitate refunds to investors.
The Committee examined claims relating to the three residential projects and classified the allottees into five categories based on the mode and extent of payment and the timing of transactions.
The Court accepted the Committee's categorisation and recommendations, with certain modifications.
• Category I: Allottees who paid the entire consideration through banking channels will receive sale certificates/NOCs within eight weeks.
Those without possession certificates will also be issued them.
• Category II: Allottees who paid more than 50% through banking channels will be allowed to pay the outstanding amount and obtain sale certificates.
Failure to pay within the prescribed period will result in the plot being treated as unsold and the verified amount being refunded under Category III.
• Category III: Those who paid less than 50% through banking channels will receive refunds with 8% interest within three months of the successful auction of the plot.
• Category IV: Claims involving cash payments will not be processed for allotment or refund through the Committee.

I: Allottees who paid the entire consideration through banking channels will receive sale certificates/NOCs within eight weeks.
Those without possession certificates will also be issued them.
Failure to pay within the prescribed period will result in the plot being treated as unsold and the verified amount being refunded under Category III.

Accepting the recommendations of the Committee, constituted to oversee the liquidation of PACL's assets and refund of investors, with certain modifications, a bench of Justice Pamidighantam Sri Narasimha and Justice Atul S. Chandurkar also directed that allottees who paid less than 50% of the consideration through banking channels be refunded their verified payments with 8% interest after the concerned plots are successfully auctioned.
The dispute arose from SEBI's action against PACL for allegedly operating an unregistered Collective Investment Scheme.
In 2016, the Supreme Court constituted a committee headed by former Chief Justice of India R.M. Lodha to liquidate PACL's land assets and facilitate refunds to investors.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Directs Probe Into Why Registry Refused To List ED Plea Against Bail For Over Three Years
stories.title: Supreme Court Directs Probe Into Why Registry Refused To List ED Plea Against Bail For Over Three Years
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday(November 20) directed its Secretary General to conduct a fact-finding enquiry and submit a report explaining why a petition filed by the Enforcement Directorate in 2023 challenging a bail order was not listed for hearing for more than three years despite a judicial direction.

The bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana was hearing a petition filed by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) against the grant of bail to Raman Singla.
Notice in the matter had been issued in 2023, yet the case was never listed for over three years.
"Why has this matter not been listed?
September 2023, September 2024, September 2025, September 2026.
This is what I want to know," CJI Surya Kant asked at the outset.
Justice Bagchi described that situation as "institutional lethargy."

Senior Advocate Siddharth Dave, appearing for Singla, said that such a situation should not occur in the Supreme Court and that the Registry “can't be managed like that.” Dave remarked that he had “never seen this happen in the Supreme Court.”
"Maybe because you have not been in the Supreme Court Registry," retorted Senior Advocate Zoheb Hossain, who was representing the ED.
"I have been here twice the number of years you have practised, Mr Hossain," responded Dave.
"As an Advocate-on-Record I mean," Hossain clarified.
"Since 1990, I have been practising.

stories.headline: Ahead of demolition, Army Welfare Housing Organisation begins takeover of Chander Kunj flats in Kochi
stories.title: Ahead of demolition, Army Welfare Housing Organisation begins takeover of Chander Kunj flats in Kochi
stories.summary: Last month, a Single Bench of Kerala High Court directed AWHO to take possession of apartments from residents and hand them over to Edifice Engineering, company entrusted with the demolition work
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Army Welfare Housing Organisation (AWHO) has begun taking over apartments in Chander Kunj Army Towers ‘B’ and ‘C’ at Silver Sand Island, Vyttila, in Kochi, ahead of their demolition.

A Single Bench of the Kerala High Court had last month directed the AWHO to take possession of the apartments from the residents and hand them over to Edifice Engineering, the company entrusted with the demolition work.

The takeover, originally scheduled to begin on October 5, 2026, and be completed within a fortnight, as decided by a committee headed by the District Collector, was stalled after the AWHO challenged the decision in the High Court.
Apartment owners from across the State had turned up to hand over their flats in response to a notice issued by the apartment association, but could not do so.
“We have issued fresh notices to apartment owners regarding the takeover.
However, the actual demolition can begin only after the demolition contract with Edifice Engineering is finalised.

The district administration has shared a revised draft agreement, which is likely to be finalised at the next meeting of the Collector’s committee,” said Saji Thomas, president of the Chander Kunj Army Towers Apartment Owners Association (CATAOA).
The apartments are being taken over in the presence of the Kanayannur tahsildar before being handed over to Edifice Engineering.
More than 20 apartment owners who have shifted to rented accommodation turned up to hand over the keys to their flats.

The AWHO has already taken possession of around 50 apartments belonging to owners who opted for the buy-back option instead of receiving newly constructed apartments in replacement for the demolished ones.

Originally, the plan was to hand over the apartment keys along with an affidavit signed by the AWHO and countersigned by the tahsildar, affirming the organisation’s undertaking to provide reconstructed apartments in place of the existing ones.
However, this arrangement was dropped on Friday.
